38-024.r: Communist Party of India split into CPI and CPI(M) → 1964.

38-025.r: Year of establishment → CPI(M) 1964; CPI 1925; Bahujan Samaj Party 1984; All India Trinamool Congress 1998.

38-026.r: Order of founding → Telugu Desam Party (1982) → Bahujan Samaj Party (14 April 1984) → Samajwadi Party (1992) → Trinamool Congress (1 January 1998).
38-026.h: Read it as T-B-S-T: Telugu, Bahujan, Samajwadi, Trinamool.

38-027.r: Trade union links → Bhartiya Majdoor Sangh: BJP; INTUC: Congress; AITUC: CPI; UTUC: Revolutionary Socialist Party.
38-027.c: Option (b) fits three pairs, but UTUC is linked to the Revolutionary Socialist Party, not CPI(M), whose union is CITU; so the book marks none.

38-028.r: Not in the United Front Government (1996-97) → Bahujan Samaj Party, Haryana Vikas Party, Samata Party; Asom Gana Parishad was a part.

38-030.r: 2004 Lok Sabha (14th) → Congress 145, BJP 138 (not 133), CPI(M) 43 (not 48) → only statement 1 correct.

38-031.r: Wrong pair: TDP won 29 seats in 13th Lok Sabha, not 30. Correct: CPM 32, BSP 14, BJD 10.

38-032.r: 1989 Lok Sabha → Congress largest (197 seats) but no majority; Janata Dal govt under V.P. Singh with outside BJP and Left support; 'Congress System' ended → both true.

38-033.r: BJP-led coalition's National Agenda → policy guidance, promises, guiding principles; coalition must respect all partners; both A and R true, but R does not explain A.

38-034.r: Kerala → no regional party in power: Congress or CPI(M), both national parties, rule by turns. J&K is now a UT (Reorganisation Act, 2019).

38-035.r: Indian governments rest on majority of seats, not of votes (A true); first-past-the-post decides by relative majority of votes (R true) → R explains A.

38-036.r: 33% seats for women in legislatures → needs Constitutional Amendment (Arts 330 to 334 have no women quota) (A false); parties can give women 33% tickets without one (R true).

38-037.r: No fixed party system in India (A) because there are too many parties (R) → both true, R explains A; casteism, regionalism and socio-economic factors also add parties.

38-038.r: Party system → a part of the political system; parties form and run governments in a democracy.

38-039.r: India has a written Constitution (A true); strong regional parties reflect regional aspirations (R true); R does not explain A.

38-040.r: Pressure group → organised group that does not contest elections but influences policy, e.g., trade unions, farmers', women's and business organisations.

38-041.r: Inner-party democracy → periodic elections within the party to choose its office-bearers.

38-042.r: 'One-party dominant system' for India's early years → Rajni Kothari (books: Politics in India, Caste in Indian Politics, Rethinking Democracy).

38-043.r: Anti-defection Bill → passed 15 February 1985, in force 1 March 1985; 52nd Amendment added 10th Schedule and amended Arts 101, 102, 190, 191.

38-044.r: Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985) → covers en-bloc defections, smaller defections in one spell, and voting to topple or support a government; not large defections in several spells.

38-045.r: Political parties first got constitutional recognition in 1985, when the 10th Schedule (anti-defection) was added.

38-046.r: Merger of parties recognised under anti-defection law → when at least two-thirds of the legislature party agree to it.

38-047.r: Defection disqualification (Tenth Schedule) → decided by Speaker or Chairman, not the President; 'political party' is mentioned in the Tenth Schedule → neither statement correct.
38-047.t: The President decides other MP disqualifications; defection cases go to the presiding officer.

38-048.r: Anti-defection law → nominated member disqualified only if he joins a party after six months (1 false); no time-limit for presiding officer to decide (2 true).

38-049.r: Speaker may be disqualified if he later joins another party (statement d untrue). Exempt: leaving party on becoming Speaker; merger. Absence from a vote can disqualify.

38-050.r: Defection exception → presiding officer who gives up party membership on election, or rejoins it after leaving office → both conditions.

38-051.r: Anti-Defection Law as early as 1979 → Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly.

38-052.r: Votes-seats mismatch (Karnataka 1994: Janata Dal 36% votes, 116 seats; BJP 20.4%, 40 seats; Congress 31%, 35 seats) → first-past-the-post system.

38-053.r: Recognised Opposition party in Lok Sabha → at least 1/10 of total members, i.e., 54 of 543.

38-054.r: 'Bhu-Poratam' (land struggle) → Andhra Pradesh; Communist parties (Bharatiya Khet Mazdoor Union) sought land and house sites for landless farm workers.

38-055.r: Communist Party's social base → agricultural and industrial workers, the educated, youth; not the business class, which supports capitalism.

38-056.r: Kamaraj Plan (1963, K. Kamaraj, Congress President) → to make the Indian National Congress vibrant.

38-057.r: Electoral Bond Scheme (2 January 2018) → aim transparency; bond valid 15 days; credited same day; parties need 1% votes, not 2% → A, C, D correct.

39-001.r: Art 368 → Parliament can amend any part by addition, variation or repeal, except basic structure (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973); Parliament is supreme elected body → R explains A.

39-002.r: Article 368(1) → Parliament may amend any provision by addition, variation or repeal → all three.

39-003.r: Constitution Amendment Bill (Article 368) → must be passed by each House separately by special majority, then presented to the President for assent.

39-006.r: Amendment Bill → introduced in either House of Parliament [Art 368(2)], not in State legislatures; special majority in each House; procedure taken from South Africa.

39-009.r: Amendment sent to States for ratification [Art 368(2)] → a State Assembly may pass or reject the resolution but cannot propose amendments to it → all three.

39-010.r: Ratification by half the States needed for → federal provisions, Supreme Court and High Courts, Art 368 itself. New States, boundaries, names → simple majority of Parliament.

39-012.r: Half-States ratification needed for Art 279A (GST Council), also Arts 54, 55, 73, 162, 241, Seventh Schedule lists, States' representation; not Arts 53, 239A, 243A.

39-013.r: Half-States ratification → needed for Union List (Seventh Schedule) and extent of State executive power (Art 162); not for conditions of Governor's office (Art 158).

39-015.r: Outside the Art 368 State-ratification list → President's qualification, conditions of office and tenure; executive powers, courts, President's election, legislative powers, States' representation are inside.

39-016.r: First amendment ratified by State legislatures under Art 368(2) → Third Amendment, 1954 (re-enacted entry 33 of Concurrent List).

39-017.r: Rajya Sabha rejects a Constitution Amendment Bill passed by Lok Sabha → Bill is dropped; there is no joint sitting for amendment bills.
39-017.t: Joint sitting applies to ordinary bills, never to Constitution Amendment Bills.

39-018.r: Amendment bill → no prior President's recommendation (1 false); President must give assent (2 true); passed by both Houses by special majority, no joint sitting (3 true).

39-019.r: Art 368 → two methods (special majority; plus half-States ratification) (i true); initiated in either House (ii false); no joint sitting (iii false); President cannot veto (iv true).

39-020.r: President's veto on amendment bills removed by 24th Amendment ('shall give his assent'). 44th Amendment, 1978 → President may return ministers' advice for reconsideration (Art 74).

39-021.r: Article 368 amended by 24th Amendment, 1971 (Parliament can amend any part incl. FRs; President must assent) and 101st Amendment, 2016 (for GST) → both true.

39-022.r: First Constitution Amendment Bill → 1951; added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule; amended Arts 15, 19 and others.

39-023.r: First Amendment, 1951 → protection of agrarian (land) reforms in certain States; added Arts 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule.

39-025.r: Ninth Schedule → added by First Amendment Act, 1951 (shields Acts from FR challenge). Tenth Schedule → Fifty-second Amendment, 1985. Original Constitution: 395 Articles, 8 Schedules.

39-026.r: First Amendment (1951) → passed to overcome court rulings on Fundamental Rights: added Art 15(4), new limits in Art 19 (public order, friendly relations, incitement), Ninth Schedule.

39-027.r: 15th Amendment, 1963 → SC Judge's age decided by authority and manner Parliament provides by law. 16th (1963) → anti-secession; 18th (1966) → clarified 'State' in Art 3.

39-028.r: Privy purses and special rights of former princely rulers → abolished by 26th Amendment, 1971.

39-029.r: 13th Amendment → Nagaland; 18th → clarified 'State'; 39th → elections of President, VP, Speaker, PM beyond court challenge; 52nd → anti-defection law.

39-030.r: 38th Amendment → curbed judicial review; 44th → Right to Property removed as FR; 61st → voting age 21 to 18; 42nd → 'Secular' added to Preamble.

39-031.r: 69th Amendment (1991) → Delhi as NCT; 75th (1994) → State Rent Tribunals; 80th (2000) → 10th Finance Commission advice; 83rd (2000) → no SC quota in Arunachal Panchayats.

39-032.r: Cooperatives under Art 19(1)(c) → 97th (2011); SC/ST backlog vacancies → 81st (2000); NJAC → 99th (2014, struck down 16 October 2015); Council of Ministers size → 91st (2003).

39-033.c: Question asks year of implementation, but these are enactment years (86th effective 1.4.2010); the code (d) still fits.

39-034.r: 'Mini Constitution' → 42nd Amendment (1976); it sought to overcome the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) ruling on essential features.

39-035.r: 42nd Amendment (1976) → added 'socialist, secular, integrity' to Preamble and 10 Fundamental Duties (not eight). Incorrect: statements 2 and 3 (the new Directive Principles list).

39-036.r: Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment, 1976 (Swaran Singh Committee); Part IV-A, Art 51A; first 10, now 11; idea from the Soviet Constitution.

39-037.r: 44th Amendment (1978, Janata Govt) → undid 42nd changes; President can return ministers' advice for reconsideration only once. 42nd had bound President to ministers' advice (Art 74).

39-039.r: PM's election beyond judicial review → 39th Amendment (1975), undone by 44th (1978): 1 false. SC struck down 99th Amendment (NJAC, 2014) for judicial independence: 2 true.
